title: SCIM safe-lock deprovision state machine and idempotent retry playbook
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Problem: SCIM deprovisioning currently experiences two classes of failures seen in recent incidents: (1) duplicate or conflicting operations when a user is re-created during a deprovision window, producing ghost accounts or stale role bindings; (2) retry storms and non-idempotent replays that surface as double-deletes or inconsistent group membership. These issues impact RBAC v2 integrity and make audit trails noisy for compliance teams.

Proposal: Implement a 'safe-lock' state machine for SCIM user/group deprovision flows plus an idempotent retry playbook. Key ideas: a short-lived deprovision lock (TTL'd) per subject that records operation_id and initiator; state transitions (queued -> draining -> locked -> tombstoned -> deleted) with explicit audit events at each step; idempotency tokens on incoming SCIM requests; dead-lettering for non-transient failures; and an adaptive retry/backoff policy that coordinates across worker pools to avoid replay storms.

This ticket covers the design and incremental implementation of the state machine, the audit log schema additions required, the idempotency token validation, and the rollout & monitoring plan. Integration points with RBAC v2: deprovision transitions must check role binding cleanup policies and should not finalize deletion until mandatory owner/role handoff or automated removal rules are satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: SCIM deprovision flows emit the following audit events: deprov.requested, deprov.lock_acquired, deprov.draining, deprov.tombstoned, deprov.finalized with request_id and initiator
Replaying the same SCIM request (same idempotency token) is a no-op and returns the original response status with proof request_id
Deprovision lock TTL prevents concurrent deletes for at least 15 minutes and is configurable per-org
False-deprovision incidents (user reappears immediately after delete) reduced to <0.5% of total deprovisions in the first 30 days
Metrics surfaced in Console: deprov_latency_p50/p95, deprov_false_positive_rate, deprov_deadletter_count
implementation_plan: 1) Add deprov_lock table (org_id, subject_id, operation_id, ttl, initiator, created_at)
2) Extend SCIM service to require idempotency-token header and persist operation_id per request
3) Implement server-side state machine transitions and emit new audit events to Audit Service
4) Add dedupe layer in worker queue to avoid parallel workers processing same subject_id
5) Implement dead-letter queue with retention and manual replay tooling for SE/Support
6) Add config to Console for org-level deprov_lock_ttl and soft-delete policies
7) Release with opt-in flag for a subset of orgs, monitor for 72h, then expand
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 3 low-risk orgs (internal + 2 customers) for 1 week
Stage: expand to 25% of orgs with high SCIM volume for 2 weeks
General availability: global flip after metrics and audits meet success criteria
Rollback: remove opt-in flag and pause new deprovision finalizations while re-enqueueing in legacy path
migration_notes: Existing in-flight deprovision operations at rollout should be reconciled by the reconcile job which will backfill lock records for operations younger than 24h. For users with repeated add/remove cycles, the reconcile job will annotate audit entries with conflict_resolution:reconciled. Communication: update API deprecation/behavior docs and notify customers 7 days prior to GA.
